messages.subject: ddply summarize "sum" characters
parts:
When using summarize, is there a way to get a concatenation of a character column? For example, this gives me a data frame with the sum of the sales by Territory, Month, and Product
test <- ddply(input, 
              c("Territory", "Month", "Product"), 
              summarize,
              Sales = sum(Sales, na.rm = TRUE))
              
but can I get another column that would tell me the states of these sales? I have tried:
test <- ddply(input, 
              c("Territory", "Month", "Product"), 
              summarize,
              Sales = sum(Sales, na.rm = TRUE),
              State = unique(State))

messages.author: 27405c4b711a1080
messages.subject: Re: ddply summarize "sum" characters
parts:
Seems like you want to group_by(State). 

input %>%
group_by(State) %>%
ddply(.,

c("Territory", "Month", "Product"), 
              summarize,
              Sales = sum(Sales, na.rm = TRUE),

)

If that doesn't work, send some data to play with. 

B

On Fri, Sep 11, 2015 at 1:38 PM, Tan Chen <tanta...@gmail.com> wrote:
Territory State Month Product Sales 
D09709   NJ       8        Tab      12
D09709   NY       8        Tab      12
D09709   CT       8        MED    12
D09709   NJ       8        MED     12

Does this do what you want? 

require(dplyr)
input <- data.frame(Territory = c("D09709","D09709","D09709","D09709"), State = c("NJ", "NY", "CT", "NJ"), Month = rep(8, 4), Product = c("Tab", "Tab", "MED", "MED"), Sales = rep(12, 4))

input %>%
group_by(Territory, Month, Product) %>%
summarise(Sales = sum(Sales, na.rm=TRUE), State = paste(State, collapse = " "))

Comic sans because you made me type out your data frame. Use dput() next time. 

B

messages.author: 0c39e60ddb38622b
messages.subject: Re: ddply summarize "sum" characters
parts:
Hi:

dput() is a function that takes an R object as input and returns a
text-based representation of it that can be copied and pasted into
e-mails to R-related mailing lists. The advantage of this way of
sending data is that a potential helpeR is assured that when the
dput() output is copied and pasted into an R session, the structure of
that object is identical to the one on your computer.

Example:

set.seed(53490)
DF <- data.frame(x = c("A", "B", "A", "B"),
y = rpois(4, 10))

> DF # Don't send this...
x y
1 A 8
2 B 9
3 A 11
4 B 10
> str(DF)
'data.frame': 4 obs. of 2 variables:
$ x: Factor w/ 2 levels "A","B": 1 2 1 2
$ y: int 8 9 11 10
>
> dput(DF) # Send the output of this
structure(list(x = structure(c(1L, 2L, 1L, 2L), .Label = c("A",
"B"), class = "factor"), y = c(8L, 9L, 11L, 10L)), .Names = c("x",
"y"), row.names = c(NA, -4L), class = "data.frame")

If you copy and paste the output from dput() into your R session,
assign it to an object DF and type DF; str(DF), you should find that
it is identical to the output given above. In other words, there is no
ambiguity over whether or not x is a factor or a character vector.
The object you entered is identical to the one I sent.

You are now informed about dput(), and hopefully others are as well :)

You're welcome, Brandon ;D

Dennis
